item.title: Stanford University Sees Surge in Catholic Converts Through OCIA
item.dc:creator: Julia Torres
item.description:
At Stanford University, the Catholic Community at Stanford (CC@S) has experienced a significant increase in adults entering the Catholic Church through the Order of Christian Initiation of Adults (OCIA). In 2026, 46 candidates were received into full communion, compared to an average of four per year over the past three decades. This growth reflects a shift towards traditional worship and a search for stability and meaning among young adults. Dominican friars, who have served the university for over 35 years, have adapted their ministry to focus more on the student community, emphasizing the beauty and tradition of Catholic worship. Stanford professor James Sonne highlights the vibrancy of the Catholic community as a sign of a new springtime for the Church, rooted in hope and mercy. More: EWTN News

item.title: Portland Archbishop Outlines Plan for Spiritual Renewal
item.dc:creator: Zelda Caldwell
item.description:
Archbishop Alexander Sample of Portland, Oregon, has proposed an ambitious plan for spiritual renewal in his archdiocese, calling on all Catholics to embrace a ‘Christ-centered and kerygmatic’ mission. Inspired by Pope Leo XIV’s emphasis on mission over maintenance, Sample’s pastoral letter, ‘Go Therefore and Make Disciples,’ encourages practical steps for priests, Catholic schools, and lay faithful. The letter focuses on priestly holiness, daily Mass, and fostering a sense of fraternity among clergy. Additionally, it aims to reform Catholic schools to better align with the mission of evangelization, following previous initiatives to eliminate gender ideology and promote traditional liturgical practices. More: National Catholic Register

item.title: Exorcising Halloween: A Catholic Teacher’s Quest to Understand and Defend Allhallowtide
item.dc:creator: Charles Fraune
item.description:
For ten years, a Catholic high school theology teacher struggled to explain the significance of Halloween to his students. In his recent book, ‘Exorcising Halloween,’ he addresses the corruption of the holiday, attributing it to the work of Freemasonry and the decline of Catholic faith. The author emphasizes the importance of celebrating Christ the King and All Saints to counteract the occult symbolism and fear associated with Halloween. He argues that understanding and promoting the true meaning of these feasts can help restore their honor and dignity in the Church. More: OnePeterFive

item.title: Bishop Mutsaerts Discusses the Catholic Church’s Response to Crisis
item.dc:creator: Edward Pentin
item.description:
Bishop Mutsaerts of ’s-Hertogenbosch addressed the Catholic Identity Conference in Pittsburgh, discussing the current crisis in the Church. He noted that while traditional Catholics see the Church as experiencing an unprecedented springtime, others view it differently based on statistics. The bishop emphasized the need for faith, doctrine, and courage, rather than nostalgia or panic. He warned against the tendency to reform everything, arguing that the Church’s task is to preserve and deepen what has been received from Christ, not to innovate for innovation’s sake. He concluded that any reform should ultimately help people become holier. More: Edward Pentin

item.title: Psychologist Manfred Lütz Debunks Misunderstandings of Mental Illness in Church Context
item.dc:creator: info@domradio.de (DOMRADIO.DE)
item.description:
Psychiatrist and theologian Manfred Lütz argues in his new book that not every crisis or sadness is a mental illness. He warns against pathologizing normal human weaknesses and suggests that religion can provide orientation. Lütz uses the example of Saint Francis of Assisi, questioning whether his hearing voices might have been considered schizophrenia today, but argues that his abilities were not a disease. He advocates for finding fulfillment through meaningful actions and social connections, emphasizing the importance of the Christian faith in providing a sense of purpose beyond mere practicality. More: Domradio

item.title: Two German Theologians Join Vatican’s International Theological Commission
item.dc:creator: info@domradio.de (DOMRADIO.DE)
item.description:
The Vatican has appointed Jan-Heiner Tück and Bernhard Knorn as dogmaticians to its International Theological Commission, a group of 24 theologians advising the Pope on theological matters. Tück teaches at the University of Vienna and focuses on Jewish-Christian dialogue and the relationship between literature and theology, while Knorn, a Jesuit, teaches at the Philosophical-Theological High School in Frankfurt and specializes in ecumenical dialogue and conciliar history. The commission, established in 1969 by Pope Paul VI, includes four women among its new members and addresses current theological debates and issues at the request of the Pope or the Holy See, particularly the Office of the Faith. Recent topics have included the ethics of human interaction with nature. More: Domradio

item.title: Apostolic Nuncio Urges Human-Centered Approach to Technology at G20 Interfaith Forum
item.dc:creator: Madalaine Elhabbal
item.description:
Archbishop Gabriele Caccia, apostolic nuncio to the United States, urged attendees at the G20 Interfaith Forum in Salt Lake City to advocate for technology that promotes human flourishing. Caccia highlighted the need for judgment to ensure progress serves the human person. Vatican Secretary of State Cardinal Pietro Parolin, on behalf of Pope Leo XIV, expressed hope for the forum to exemplify human solidarity and called for respect in discussions. The forum also included discussions on overcoming political divisions and promoting interfaith cooperation. More: EWTN News

item.title: Pope Leo XIV Expands International Theological Commission with New Members
item.dc:creator: Unknown
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV has appointed 24 new members and confirmed 6 others for the International Theological Commission, bringing the total to 30 members. The Commission, which began its 2026-2031 term, now includes increased representation from Asia, Africa, and South America. The appointments reflect a diverse range of backgrounds and include more lay members, particularly women. The Commission assists the Holy See in examining doctrinal questions and publishes documents with the approval of the Prefect of the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith. More: Vatican News

item.title: Milan Diocese Prepares for World Youth Day with Buddhist Course
item.dc:creator: Luigi Casalini
item.description:
The Diocese of Milan is organizing a five-lesson online course titled ‘Sui passi del Buddha’ to prepare participants for the 2027 World Youth Day in Seoul. The course, promoted by the Carlo Maria Martini Center in collaboration with the University of Milan-Bicocca, aims to introduce the history, thought, and various traditions of Buddhism. It is part of the diocese’s efforts to understand Buddhism’s origins and relevance in today’s world, particularly for young Catholics. Critics argue that this approach, while innovative, may divert attention from the core teachings of Christianity. More: Messainlatino

item.title: Parolin Under Scrutiny: Controversy Over ‘Pontificate to Reajust’ and Recent Setbacks
item.dc:creator: johan
item.description:
Cardinal Pietro Parolin’s statement that Pope Leo XIV might ‘reajust’ his pontificate after the operation has caused controversy in the Vatican. The Secretary of State’s remarks, made at an event, were described as ‘unfortunate’ by Vaticanist Nico Spuntoni, who noted Parolin’s recent series of setbacks, including his role in the Russia mission, opposition to the Domus Paul VI lease, and failure to secure the deanship of the College of Cardinals. Spuntoni suggests Parolin carries the ‘stigma of the defeated’ in the conclave and expects a meeting between the Pope and Parolin to clarify the situation. More: InfoVaticana
